summary: Reproduced the chunked-prefill progress reset in the actual scheduler/cache implementation: with skip_radix_cache_insert, three scheduling rounds started at token offsets [0, 0, 0]. The fix separates radix publication from unfinished-request bookkeeping, preserving request-owned KV progress while leaving the protected tree boundary unchanged for final cleanup. The regression now advances [0, 8, 16], does not call radix insertion, and covers ChunkCache independently.

tests.what_was_measured: Three failures: chunk scheduling restarted at [0, 0, 0], RadixCache prefix_indices stayed length 2 instead of 6, and ChunkCache prefix_indices stayed length 2 instead of 6. Raw output: reports/j-0dedc5380f38/regression-before.txt

Three regression and boundary tests passed after the fix, including scheduler progress, no radix publication, request-owned final cleanup, and ChunkCache progress. Raw output: reports/j-0dedc5380f38/regression-final.txt
42 related tests and 61 subtests passed. Raw output: reports/j-0dedc5380f38/related-tests.txt
A float32 matrix product executed on the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 and exactly matched the independent CPU result. Raw output: reports/j-0dedc5380f38/gpu-torch-check.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: ROCm reported one idle assigned AMD Instinct MI350X with gfx950; a Torch ROCm matrix multiplication ran on it and exactly matched CPU (sum 12976.0). This is environment evidence only, not a full HTTP/model reproduction. See gpu-inventory.txt and gpu-torch-check.txt.

remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B weights were not present, so the original full-model HTTP crash was not rerun.
The deterministic tiny-Llama fixture was inspected but not used to claim model-architecture or semantic validation.
The C++ radix backend change was syntax-checked through Python compilation but its optional native extension was not rebuilt; this task changes only Python bookkeeping and no native source.
